chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man looks down upon a people, overlooking them, or looks at them from a crack in something of theirs, and they throw something at him and hit him, so they kill him or blind his eye, then there is no penalty (blood money) upon them.

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, a man peeked from a crack in the chamber of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came with an arrow to blind his eye, but he found him to have gone away. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
O the filthy one! By Allah, if he had remained for me, I would have blinded his two eyes.

key_terms.اطلع: to look down upon or peek into

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on killing or blinding a person who spies on you from a private area?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *ghurm* (compensation) exemption for those killed or blinded while spying, rooted in the right to defend one's privacy (*khass*). It cites the precedent of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) who intended to blind a spy peeking into his chamber, illustrating that the observed party holds the right to use defensive force without incurring liability. This ruling underscores the sanctity of private spaces in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between public visibility and private seclusion.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’la Bin Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a man emerges upon a people to overlook upon them, or look at them from a crack of something of them, so they pelt him and it hits him, so he is either killed or blinds his eye, so there is no penalty upon them’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man peeked at Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> from a crack of his<sup>saww</sup> chamber, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> came over with an arrow in order to poke his eyes, so he<sup>saww</sup> found him to have gone away. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
Where is the filthy one? But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, had he remained for me<sup>saww</sup>, I<sup>saww</sup> would have poked his eyes’.
